title: Earthquake Wave Propagation on 3D Globe
prompt:
Create a 3D interactive earthquake wave propagation simulator on a globe using Three.js. Users click on the globe to trigger earthquakes and watch seismic P-waves and S-waves propagate across the surface. The entire application must be in a single HTML file.

## Three.js Import
Use this importmap in <head>:
<script type="importmap">
{ "imports": {
    "three": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js",
    "three/addons/": "https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/examples/jsm/"
} }
</script>
Then in <script type="module">:
import * as THREE from 'three';
import { OrbitControls } from 'three/addons/controls/OrbitControls.js';

## Scene Setup
- Background 0x000011 (deep space).
- PerspectiveCamera at (0, 0, 20), looking at origin.
- OrbitControls enabled, enableDamping=true.
- Ambient light (0x223344, intensity 0.3), directional light (0xffffff, intensity 0.8) at (10, 10, 10).

## Globe
- A sphere (radius 6, 128x64 segments) as the Earth.
- Apply a procedural color map: generate land (greens/browns) and ocean (blues) using 3D noise. Sample noise at each vertex's position to decide land (noise > threshold) vs ocean.
- Add a subtle wireframe overlay with thin white lines (opacity 0.05) for latitude/longitude grid.
- The globe rotates slowly (0.1 rad/s) by default.

## Earthquake Mechanics
- Click on the globe surface (raycaster) to place an earthquake epicenter.
- Each earthquake generates two wave fronts:
  - **P-wave**: faster (speed 6 units/sec on surface), shown as expanding ring in blue (0x4488ff), decays over time.
  - **S-wave**: slower (speed 3.5 units/sec on surface), shown as expanding ring in red (0xff4444), decays over time.
- Wave fronts are rendered as expanding torus-like rings conforming to the sphere surface (use shader or geometry deformation).
- Each ring has amplitude that decays exponentially with distance from epicenter: amplitude = A0 * exp(-0.15 * distance).
- Displace the globe vertices radially by the sum of all active wave amplitudes at that vertex.
- Support up to 5 simultaneous active earthquakes. Older ones fade out after 10 seconds.
- At the epicenter, place a small pulsing yellow sphere (radius 0.15).

## Controls
- Click on globe to place earthquake.
- Press 'C' to clear all earthquakes.
- Press Space to pause/play.
- Press 'A' to toggle auto-rotate.
- Slider (id='slider-magnitude', range 1 to 9, step 0.5, default 5) for next earthquake magnitude (affects amplitude A0 = magnitude * 0.05).
- Slider (id='slider-wave-speed', range 0.5 to 3.0, step 0.1, default 1.0) for wave speed multiplier.

## HUD (id='hud')
- Active quakes (id='hud-quakes'): number of active earthquakes
- Latest magnitude (id='hud-magnitude'): magnitude of last placed quake, 1 decimal
- P-wave radius (id='hud-pwave'): largest P-wave radius of latest quake, 1 decimal
- S-wave radius (id='hud-swave'): largest S-wave radius of latest quake, 1 decimal
- Auto-rotate (id='hud-rotate'): 'ON' or 'OFF'
- Paused (id='hud-paused'): 'Playing' or 'Paused'

## State Management
Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame:
- `activeQuakes`: number (0-5)
- `latestMagnitude`: number (rounded to 1 decimal)
- `latestPWaveRadius`: number (rounded to 2 decimals)
- `latestSWaveRadius`: number (rounded to 2 decimals)
- `autoRotate`: boolean
- `isPaused`: boolean
- `magnitude`: number (slider value)
- `waveSpeedMultiplier`: number
- `frameCount`: number
- `globeValid`: boolean (no NaN in displaced vertices)
- `totalWaveEnergy`: number (sum of all active wave amplitudes, rounded to 3 decimals)

Ensure the animation loop updates __3D_STATE__ every frame before rendering.
physics_constraints: P-waves must propagate faster than S-waves. Wave amplitude must decay with distance from epicenter. Vertex displacement must be finite (no NaN/Inf). Maximum 5 active earthquakes. Waves propagate along sphere surface (great circle distance). Higher magnitude = larger amplitude.
